summary: Reviewed precheck_multi_pusher_authority.py thoroughly: passive/active/obstructing roles come from normal_ratio = cos(true_alpha) = dot(n_in, move_dir) and heuristic thresholds (passive_ratio default 0.25, speed_floor 0.003), not from friction cone math. DEFAULT_OBJECT_FRICTION (0.8) only loads PyBullet geometry. Conceptual link to Lynch friction/motion cone exists via normal vs tangential velocity decomposition (tangential_authority = |vr_ff|*sin(alpha)), but no mu-based slip check is implemented—unlike test_single_pusher_diffdrive.py which builds segments with ±mu*Fn tangential forces. Live multi-pusher tests reuse normal_ratio for obstructing detection only; planned passive/active distinction is force-sensor based per code TODO.
current_status: Analysis complete: precheck is kinematic authority diagnostic; friction-informed threshold would be |normal_ratio| >= 1/sqrt(1+mu^2) (~0.78 for mu=0.8) vs current permissive 0.25. No code changes made.
